messages.manual.quick-start.caption: Select series on the left, tools on the right, and interact with the image in the center.
messages.manual.quick-start.section0.title: 1. Open images
messages.manual.quick-start.section0.body: Click **Open images** to select folders, files and archives together, or drop them into the window. Use the adjacent PACS browser to import from a server.
messages.manual.quick-start.section1.title: 2. Choose a view
messages.manual.quick-start.section1.body: Double-click a series for **2D**, or select it and click **MPR, 3D or Tiles**. Hover to see button names. Disabled entries indicate unsupported data.
messages.manual.quick-start.section2.title: 3. Start working
messages.manual.quick-start.section2.body: Activate an image viewport, then choose a tool on the right. **Workspace, Manual and Settings** are at the bottom left. Switching tabs preserves your work.
messages.manual.workspace.title: Workspaces and tabs
messages.manual.workspace.summary: Organize tabs and windows; save and restore your workspace.
messages.manual.workspace.caption: Saving a temporary workspace and enabling auto recovery.
messages.manual.workspace.section0.title: Open and save
messages.manual.workspace.section0.body: Importing images starts a temporary workspace automatically. Choose **Workspace → Save workspace…** at the bottom left. After naming it, use **Save changes** or **Save as…**. **Open workspace…** restores tabs, display settings and completed measurements, annotations, VOIs and crops. Saving a workspace includes the tabs and completed edits from **all windows**. Reopening restores every tab to the main window. Window positions and groups are not saved. The selected function and tool are restored too, such as **Measure → Curve** or **Service → FWHM**. Playback stays paused; restoration does not run calculations, exports or deletions. Unfinished drags are not restored.
messages.manual.workspace.section1.title: Auto recovery
messages.manual.workspace.section1.body: Enabled by default, it backs up changes **every 30 seconds**. Disabling it persists after restarting and does not affect manual saving. A green check means the backup is current. Hover over the status icon for its time or status. Hover over or click **Backup location** to view the full path. Choose **Copy path**, or **Open location** to dismiss the card and open the containing folder. Clicking **Recover** or **Discard** closes the workspace window. It reopens if recovery fails or source files need locating.
messages.manual.workspace.section2.title: Exit confirmation
messages.manual.workspace.section2.body: When closing a saved workspace, choose **Update, Don’t update, or Cancel**. A temporary workspace asks whether to save. Updating or saving exits only after a successful write; declining exits immediately, and Cancel returns to the app. **Remember my choice** skips future prompts; restore prompting in **Settings → Workspace → Exit confirmation**. Cancel never saves a preference.
messages.manual.workspace.section3.title: Images have moved
messages.manual.workspace.section3.body: Use **Locate…** to select the original file, folder or archive, or restore available series only. **Cancel restore** stops restoration.
messages.manual.workspace.section4.title: Keep original images
messages.manual.workspace.section4.body: **Workspace files contain no image pixels.** Keep local PACS downloads too. Recovery backups protect against unexpected exits and do not replace manual saving. Drafts and undo history are not saved.
messages.manual.local-import.title: Local import and series management
messages.manual.local-import.summary: Select files, folders and archives in one step.
messages.manual.local-import.caption: Folders, individual files and archives can be selected together.
messages.manual.local-import.section0.title: Select sources
messages.manual.local-import.section0.body: Click **Open images**, hold `Ctrl / ⌘` to select multiple items, then **Open selected**. Double-click folders to browse; with no selection, open the current folder. Enter a path and press Enter to navigate. Files need not have a .dcm extension.
messages.manual.local-import.section1.title: Supported archives
messages.manual.local-import.section1.body: **ZIP, RAR4/5, 7z and TAR** (including TGZ, TBZ2 and TXZ), plus single-file **GZ, BZ2 and XZ**. Unicode paths and solid RAR are supported without WinRAR. Decrypt encrypted archives and combine multipart archives before importing.
messages.manual.local-import.section2.title: Progress and large imports
messages.manual.local-import.section2.body: The task window shows scanning, extraction and reading progress, with cancellation. It closes immediately after a clean import. Duplicates, skipped files and cancelled imports keep their results until you click **OK**; failures also offer **Retry** and **Select again**. Import up to **100,000 files** per batch.
messages.manual.local-import.section3.title: Manage series
messages.manual.local-import.section3.body: Search by patient name or ID. Multi-select, double-click to open, or use the context menu, including on collapsed thumbnails. Repeated imports merge. Removing a series **does not delete original files**. Larger arrows expand patient and study groups. A highlighted **CT / MR / PET** badge identifies each series. The collapsed left rail retains Export, Clear, Workspace, Manual and Settings.
messages.manual.local-import.section4.title: Extraction limits
messages.manual.local-import.section4.body: Limits: 8 GiB per archived file, 32 GiB total extraction, 3 nesting levels and 512 MiB RAR dictionary. Extract larger archives first and import in batches. Canceling keeps loaded series. Extraction caches are cleared on exit; sources stay unchanged.
messages.manual.pacs.title: PACS query and import
messages.manual.pacs.summary: Query and download images from a DICOMweb server.
messages.manual.pacs.caption: Query filters, studies and series.
messages.manual.pacs.section0.title: 1. Configure a connection
messages.manual.pacs.section0.body: Enable PACS in **Settings → Sources**, enter its DICOMweb address and authentication, then **Test connection**. Credentials last for this session only.
messages.manual.pacs.section1.title: 2. Query studies
messages.manual.pacs.section1.body: Open **PACS browser**, choose a connection, then filter by patient, ID, accession, modality or date (`YYYY-MM-DD`). More filters include study UID and description.
messages.manual.pacs.section2.title: 3. Import series
messages.manual.pacs.section2.body: Select a study, check series and import. Completed imports appear in the sidebar. Studies and series have separate pagination; downloads can be canceled.
messages.manual.pacs.section3.title: Connection failed
messages.manual.pacs.section3.body: Check the connection, address, credentials and server, then retry. **DICOMweb** is supported; DIMSE querying and receiving are unavailable.
messages.manual.tabs.title: Tabs and separate windows
messages.manual.tabs.summary: Arrange tabs and compare images in separate windows.
messages.manual.tabs.section0.title: Arrange tabs
messages.manual.tabs.section0.body: **Right-click a tab** to close it, other tabs, tabs to its right or all tabs in that window. Drag with the left button to reorder; hold near either edge to scroll. **Middle-click** closes the target tab.
messages.manual.tabs.section1.title: Compare views
messages.manual.tabs.section1.body: Drop a tab outside the application windows, or choose **Open in separate window**. The new window keeps its tabs and tools; measurements, crops and undo history move with the tab. Drop onto another tab bar to merge. Press `Esc` to cancel a drag.
messages.manual.tabs.section2.title: Close or return
messages.manual.tabs.section2.body: Closing a separate window closes its tabs; other windows keep running. Use **Show main window** at the top right for series management, or **Move to main window** in the tab menu. Closing the last window uses the workspace exit confirmation.
messages.manual.tabs.section3.title: Save and restore
messages.manual.tabs.section3.body: Saving a workspace includes the tabs and completed edits from **all windows**. Reopening restores every tab to the main window. Window positions and groups are not saved.
messages.manual.2d.title: 2D basics
messages.manual.2d.summary: Browse with default gestures; selected tools take priority.
messages.manual.2d.caption: 2D viewing and windowing tools.
messages.manual.2d.section0.title: Mouse controls and slices
messages.manual.2d.section0.body: By default, **left-drag adjusts the window, right-drag zooms, and the wheel browses slices**. A selected tool such as Pan, Measure or Annotate takes priority on the left button; crosshairs and locator handles retain their left-button actions. Right-drag zoom does not switch tools or cancel unfinished measurements. The **Browse** panel jumps to the first or last page, or **10 pages** backward or forward.
messages.manual.2d.section1.title: Windowing and inversion
messages.manual.2d.section1.body: Drag with **Window** to adjust WW/WL, or enter values and press `Enter` or click **Apply**. CT accepts one decimal place; MR accepts three and adds **Auto window**. CT / MR **Invert** changes brightness polarity without changing source values or statistics. PET uses its own display range and units.
messages.manual.2d.section2.title: Zoom and orientation
messages.manual.2d.section2.body: Drag with **Pan, Zoom or Rotate**. Zoom shortcuts **1×, 2×, 5× and 10×** are absolute; 1× fits the image. The rotation panel provides 90° rotations and horizontal / vertical flips.
messages.manual.2d.section3.title: Before resetting
messages.manual.2d.section3.body: The secondary panel resets its current tool. **Reset all** restores the view and clears its corresponding measurements and annotations.
messages.manual.mpr.title: MPR and slab projections
messages.manual.mpr.summary: Explore linked axial, coronal and sagittal planes.
messages.manual.mpr.caption: Linked positioning across all three planes.
messages.manual.mpr.section0.title: Position and browse
messages.manual.mpr.section0.body: Select a regular volume and open **MPR**. Click to activate a plane, scroll through it, and drag the **crosshair center** to reposition in space. **Play** loops along the active plane’s navigation direction while retaining linked positioning in the other planes. Click again to stop. This is distinct from temporal 4D playback.
messages.manual.mpr.section1.title: Two rotation modes
messages.manual.mpr.section1.body: Drag a **crosshair line** to rotate the corresponding plane. The **3D rotation** tool rotates all three planes around their shared center. The corner position label shows **Oblique** when a plane departs from the standard patient axial, coronal or sagittal orientation, and restores the corresponding name on return. Independent 3D camera rotation does not rename planes; linked rotation updates names from the actual plane directions.
messages.manual.mpr.section2.title: Slab projection
messages.manual.mpr.section2.body: Choose **MIP, MinIP, Mean or Sum** and set the slab thickness. Colored boundary lines mark its extent.
messages.manual.mpr.section3.title: During segmentation
messages.manual.mpr.section3.body: Segmentation and VOI tools prioritize drawing and disable slab projection. Switch to a tool such as Windowing before moving or rotating crosshairs.
messages.manual.montage.title: Series tiles
messages.manual.montage.summary: Browse several slices together; double-click for detailed work.
messages.manual.montage.caption: Choose the column count at the top. Double-click a slice to open 2D.
messages.manual.montage.section0.title: Browse and arrange
messages.manual.montage.section0.body: Choose **2–6 images** per row and scroll vertically. The arrow beside the column options collapses patient, study and scan details while keeping the summary.
messages.manual.montage.section1.title: Synchronized display
messages.manual.montage.section1.body: Windowing, **color map, inversion**, pan, zoom and rotation apply to all cells, including newly loaded slices. Each cell shows only its slice number.
messages.manual.montage.section2.title: Measure in 2D
messages.manual.montage.section2.body: **Double-click a slice** to open or reuse its series in a 2D tab, keeping the slice, window and inversion. Ordinary measurements are not drawn in montage. Failed images show the reason and a Close tab button.
messages.manual.4d.title: 4D phase playback
messages.manual.4d.summary: Play a recognized multiphase series group.
messages.manual.4d.section0.title: Choose data
messages.manual.4d.section0.body: 4D requires **geometrically matching phases**, currently assembled from multiple classic single-frame series. A large slice count alone does not imply 4D support. Respiratory descriptions such as `Gated, 0.0%A` are supported after matching geometry is verified. Import all phases from the same study. RTSTRUCT objects are not image phases.
messages.manual.4d.section1.title: Play and position
messages.manual.4d.section1.body: **Play current phase slices** loops slices within the current phase; **4D Play** loops through phases at the same location. Only one mode runs at a time. The other playback button is disabled until playback stops. Click the corresponding button again to stop and keep the current location. Both modes are available in the expanded and collapsed sidebar. Manually changing phase stops slice playback. The expanded panel selects phases and **1–15 FPS** (default 2). Quad-layout 3D follows each phase and playback waits for its frame. With 3D selected, only phase playback is available; actual speed depends on loading and rendering.
messages.manual.4d.section2.title: Pause before editing
messages.manual.4d.section2.body: Phase changes preserve window, location and display transforms. Stop playback before editing. **Segmentation and VOIs are stored separately for each phase** and calculated from that phase’s voxels. Returning restores its regions; clearing affects only the current phase. Workspaces save regions for all phases. Automatic propagation, tracking and time-series curves are not provided. Measurements are isolated by slice and grid. Enhanced multiframe CT is outside the supported scope.
messages.manual.volume.title: 3D volume rendering and presets
messages.manual.volume.summary: Rotate volumes to explore spatial relationships; presets control their appearance.
messages.manual.volume.caption: A volume and its display presets.
messages.manual.volume.section0.title: Viewpoint
messages.manual.volume.section0.body: Left-drag **rotates** by default; selecting Window, Pan, Zoom or Crop assigns that operation to the left button. **Right-drag zooms**. The wheel also zooms because volume rendering has no slice pages. Choose **A/P/L/R/S/I** for standard directions. The orientation cube indicates the view direction; 3D has no corner text.
messages.manual.volume.section1.title: CT presets and table removal
messages.manual.volume.section1.body: CT starts with **AAA** and offers 20 presets, including General, MIP, XRay, bone, lung, vessel, cardiac, muscle and hardware. For **3D windowing**, drag vertically to shift the tissue range and horizontally to change its width; color and opacity change together. Reset restores the current preset. Presets change presentation and do not segment organs. Toggle **Bed removal** independently; disable it and crop if it removes anatomy. Grayscale inversion is unavailable in 3D.
messages.manual.volume.section2.title: Crop
messages.manual.volume.section2.body: Choose **Crop**, outline a region with the left button and release. **Inside removes the enclosed region; outside keeps it.** The region extends through the volume along your view. Reset crop restores the image; Reset all also disables table removal.
messages.manual.volume.section3.title: Standalone PET 3D
messages.manual.volume.section3.body: Open a PET series directly in 3D. Choose an available unit, display maximum, low threshold, color map and opacity. Defaults are **10%** threshold and **80%** opacity. Switching units preserves viewpoint and cropping.
messages.manual.volume.section4.title: Save the image
messages.manual.volume.section4.body: Cropping affects only the current tab and leaves sources unchanged. **Export PNG** saves the current 3D image. 3D DICOM export is unavailable.
messages.manual.measurement.title: Drawing lengths, angles and ROIs
messages.manual.measurement.summary: Activate a viewport, then choose a measurement tool.
messages.manual.measurement.caption: Four measurement types and control points on the selected object.
messages.manual.measurement.section0.title: Length
messages.manual.measurement.section0.body: **Press → Drag → Release** to finish a line. Length uses physical pixel spacing. Drag endpoints to adjust it.
messages.manual.measurement.section1.title: Angle
messages.manual.measurement.section1.body: Click **Start → Vertex → End**; the second point is the vertex. You can also drag the two arms in two steps. Angles range from 0–180°.
messages.manual.measurement.section2.title: Rectangle and ellipse
messages.manual.measurement.section2.body: Drag a bounding region and **release to finish**. Rectangles show width and height; ellipses show both diameters. Adjust corner handles, then release to update statistics.
messages.manual.measurement.section3.title: Draw another
messages.manual.measurement.section3.body: Completed objects stay selected and no longer follow the pointer. Drag on empty space to create another. Finish an angle's third point first.
messages.manual.measurement-edit.title: Editing, copying and undo
messages.manual.measurement-edit.summary: Select completed objects to edit or copy them.
messages.manual.measurement-edit.caption: A completed measurement selected for editing.
messages.manual.measurement-edit.section0.title: Complete and edit
messages.manual.measurement-edit.section0.body: **Release: selected and complete**, using the completed style with handles. **Click again: selected for editing**, using the draft style. Clicking alone does not change geometry. Release after dragging to finish again.
messages.manual.measurement-edit.section1.title: Adjust an object
messages.manual.measurement-edit.section1.body: Select an outline, label, card or ROI interior. Drag handles to reshape; drag an outline or interior to move the shape. Cards and shapes move independently by default. Enable linked movement and adjust font size and background transparency under **Settings → Measurement → Metrics & cards**, with a live preview. Press `Esc` to cancel an edit.
messages.manual.measurement-edit.section2.title: Copy and paste
messages.manual.measurement-edit.section2.body: Copy a selected measurement or annotation, then paste on the target slice. The independent copy is offset by 10 pixels. Across slices it retains **pixel coordinates** and recalculates with target spacing and pixels. Unfinished objects cannot be copied.
messages.manual.measurement-edit.section3.title: Undo, delete and save
messages.manual.measurement-edit.section3.body: Focus the image to undo, redo or delete selected objects. Shortcuts inside text fields edit text only. **Save your workspace before closing**, or export PNG, CSV or PDF. Original DICOM files do not store measurement objects.
messages.manual.measurement-roi.title: ROI metrics and measurement style
messages.manual.measurement-roi.summary: Read ROI dimensions and statistics, and adjust measurement appearance.
messages.manual.measurement-roi.caption: ROI dimensions and pixel statistics.
messages.manual.measurement-roi.section0.title: Dimensions and area
messages.manual.measurement-roi.section0.body: Dimensions use **mm** and area uses **mm²**. Ellipse dimensions are diameters. Area describes the whole geometric outline; it is **not valid pixel count multiplied by pixel area**.
messages.manual.measurement-roi.section1.title: Read statistics
messages.manual.measurement-roi.section1.body: **Mean** is the average, **SD** the population standard deviation, **Min / Max** the extremes and **N** valid pixel count. Values use modality pixels, resampled for MPR, rather than screen brightness.
messages.manual.measurement-roi.section2.title: Valid samples
messages.manual.measurement-roi.section2.body: Only valid pixels whose centers lie inside the outline are sampled; out-of-image and non-finite values are excluded. No valid sample displays **—**, not zero. CT uses HU; PET uses an available data unit.
messages.manual.measurement-roi.section3.title: Choose statistics
messages.manual.measurement-roi.section3.body: Toggle fields in **Settings → ROI statistics**. Width and height share a toggle and a row with area. Hiding fields does not change calculations.
messages.manual.measurement-style.title: Measurement styles
messages.manual.measurement-style.summary: Set separate styles for editing and completed objects.
messages.manual.measurement-style.caption: Independent editing and completed styles.
messages.manual.measurement-style.section0.title: Colors and line styles
messages.manual.measurement-style.section0.body: In **Settings → Measurements and annotations**, choose drawing / editing and completed colors, solid / dashed lines, width and font size. Changes apply immediately. Image zoom does not enlarge text or line widths. **Measurement precision** defaults to **2 decimal places**, with **integer, 1, 2 or 3 decimals** available. Length, angle, ROI dimensions/area/intensity, VOI volume/statistics, MTF and water QA results update together. Pixel/voxel counts stay integers; calculations and workspace data remain unrounded.
messages.manual.measurement-style.section1.title: Save and restore
messages.manual.measurement-style.section1.body: Styles save locally. **Restore defaults** resets only the current settings category. Save measurement objects separately in a workspace; saving a style does not save results.
messages.manual.annotation.title: Arrows and text arrows
messages.manual.annotation.summary: Point out image locations with arrows and labels.
messages.manual.annotation.caption: An arrow and a text arrow.
messages.manual.annotation.section0.title: Draw
messages.manual.annotation.section0.body: Choose **Annotations → Arrow / Text arrow**, then left-drag. **The release point is the arrow tip.** Enter text on the right, or select an existing arrow to change its text.
messages.manual.annotation.section1.title: Adjust
messages.manual.annotation.section1.body: Drag endpoints to change direction, or drag the object to move it. Adjust color, line width and arrow size in the panel; text arrows also have a font size.
messages.manual.annotation.section2.title: Keep results
messages.manual.annotation.section2.body: Selected objects support copy, paste, delete and undo. Completed annotations save in workspaces. PNG and measurement reports use their respective anonymization options.
messages.manual.segmentation.title: Threshold segmentation and depth
messages.manual.segmentation.summary: Define a 3D region in MPR, then quantify voxels by threshold.
messages.manual.segmentation.caption: Region drawing and statistics in CT / PET MPR.
messages.manual.segmentation.section0.title: 1. Draw a region
messages.manual.segmentation.section0.body: Enable **MPR → Threshold segmentation** for CT/PET, or **4D → Threshold segmentation** for CT. Drag a rectangle with the left mouse button and release. All three planes show the region; 4D shows only regions belonging to the current phase.
messages.manual.segmentation.section1.title: 2. Set a threshold
messages.manual.segmentation.section1.body: Choose **Absolute / %**, then enter a threshold or use the slider. Voxels **≥ the threshold** within the region are colored and counted. Check the CT/PET unit first.
messages.manual.segmentation.section2.title: 3. Set depth
messages.manual.segmentation.section2.body: Default depth is **√(width × height)**, extending both ways from the drawing plane. Direct depth adjustment selects **Manual**. Switch back to **Auto** to follow width and height.
messages.manual.segmentation.section3.title: Edit or troubleshoot
messages.manual.segmentation.section3.body: Return to the original plane. Drag the interior to move, or corners to resize. If no result appears, check position, threshold, unit and depth. **N = 0** means no valid voxels meet the criteria.
messages.manual.voi.title: VOI analysis
messages.manual.voi.summary: Draw a sphere or ellipsoid in MPR and quantify all valid voxels inside.
messages.manual.voi.caption: Region drawing and statistics in CT / PET MPR.
messages.manual.voi.section0.title: 1. Draw
messages.manual.voi.section0.body: Check **Enabled** in the **VOI** panel, drag outward from the center and release.
messages.manual.voi.section1.title: 2. Adjust
messages.manual.voi.section1.body: Return to the original plane. Drag the interior to move, the outline or handles to change radius, or enter a diameter. **Auto depth = diameter** forms a sphere; manual depth forms an ellipsoid.
messages.manual.voi.section2.title: The outline shrinks on other slices
messages.manual.voi.section2.body: The outline is the intersection of the 3D region and current plane. It shrinks away from the center and disappears outside the region. Edit on the original plane. **VOI ignores segmentation thresholds; drawing on PET MIP is unsupported.**
messages.manual.quantification.title: CT / PET quantification
messages.manual.quantification.summary: Check units first, then understand what is counted.
messages.manual.quantification.caption: Region drawing and statistics in CT / PET MPR.
messages.manual.quantification.section0.title: CT and PET units
messages.manual.quantification.section0.body: CT uses **HU**; PET uses the available SUVbw, native SUV or activity units without inventing missing SUV values. Quantitative segmentation and VOIs are available in CT/PET **MPR** and CT **4D**. 4D uses the current phase’s original voxels.
messages.manual.quantification.section1.title: Two threshold modes
messages.manual.quantification.section1.body: **Absolute** uses the current unit. **PET %** is relative to the region maximum. **CT %** interpolates between minimum and maximum: 50% of −100 to 300 HU is 100 HU.
messages.manual.quantification.section2.title: Check thresholds after changing units
messages.manual.quantification.section2.body: Display units do not change the region's independent quantitative unit. Changing a **region unit** resets absolute thresholds to SUV 2.5 or source-unit 0; set them again. Percentage values remain unchanged.
messages.manual.quantification.section3.title: Read results
messages.manual.quantification.section3.body: **MEAN / SD**: mean and standard deviation; **MIN / MAX**: extremes; **N**: voxel count; **VOL**: cm³. Segmentation counts threshold-qualified voxels; VOI counts the whole region. Without valid results, N/VOL are 0 and other values are —. Windowing and color maps do not affect statistics.
messages.manual.interaction.title: Edit segments and VOIs
messages.manual.interaction.summary: Edit, name, hide or delete segment and VOI regions.
messages.manual.interaction.section0.title: Read the cursor
messages.manual.interaction.section0.body: Image tools use **pointer + tool icon**. Segmentation / VOI interiors show Move; edges and handles show Resize. Drag outside existing regions to create another.
messages.manual.interaction.section1.title: Crosshair priority
messages.manual.interaction.section1.body: With ordinary tools, crosshair hits take priority for positioning or rotation. Enabled segmentation / VOI takes over region editing. Switch to Windowing or another tool to use crosshairs.
messages.manual.interaction.section2.title: Cancel and delete
messages.manual.interaction.section2.body: Click the image for keyboard focus. `Esc` cancels drawing or editing; `Delete / Backspace` removes the selection. Keys in input fields edit text only.
messages.manual.management.title: Region management
messages.manual.management.summary: Each tab owns its regions; 4D further isolates them by phase.
messages.manual.management.caption: Select, show, hide and delete regions in the list on the right.
messages.manual.management.section0.title: Select and name
messages.manual.management.section0.body: Click a name to select; **double-click to rename**. The left dot toggles visibility, and × deletes the item. Unchecking **Enabled** hides that region type and pauses drawing.
messages.manual.management.section1.title: Clear regions
messages.manual.management.section1.body: **Clear segmentation / Clear VOI** removes that type. **Clear all** removes both region types in the current MPR tab without affecting other tabs. **In 4D, both actions affect only the current phase**; regions in other phases remain.
messages.manual.management.section2.title: Continue later
messages.manual.management.section2.body: Regions and segmentation masks save and restore with a **workspace**; statistics can be exported in measurement reports. Binary SEG import/export and structured SR export are supported. RTSTRUCT and SR import remain unavailable. Closing unsaved tabs loses their results.
messages.manual.pet-units.title: PET display and CT/PET quantification
messages.manual.pet-units.summary: View PET and check CT/PET units, thresholds and quantitative results.
messages.manual.pet-units.caption: Standalone PET MPR with intensity and unit controls.
messages.manual.pet-units.section0.title: Standalone PET
messages.manual.pet-units.section0.body: Select a static PT series to open **2D, MPR or 3D** directly, without CT. Standalone MPR has three planes; PET/CT fusion also offers MIP.
messages.manual.pet-units.section1.title: Display range
messages.manual.pet-units.section1.body: **PET windowing** sets display range, slider maximum and unit. Only supported units appear; missing SUV information falls back to source units. Color maps and opacity change appearance only.
messages.manual.pet-units.section2.title: Independent fusion controls
messages.manual.pet-units.section2.body: **CT windowing** affects CT/FUSION; **PET windowing** affects PET/FUSION/MIP. Changing display units does not change saved regions' quantitative thresholds.
messages.manual.fusion.title: CT/PET pairing and fusion
messages.manual.fusion.summary: Verify CT and PET sources before viewing fusion.
messages.manual.fusion.caption: CT, PET, FUSION and PET MIP.
messages.manual.fusion.section0.title: 1. Choose a pair
messages.manual.fusion.section0.body: Select CT or PET, click **Fusion**, then choose the other modality; alternatively select one CT and one PET together. Candidates default to the same patient, prioritizing the same study.
messages.manual.fusion.section1.title: 2. Verify identity
messages.manual.fusion.section1.body: Check patient, study and series. Enable **Show other patients** when necessary; mismatched or uncertain identity requires manual confirmation. **Pairing does not guarantee registration.** Check anatomical alignment.
messages.manual.fusion.section2.title: 3. Browse linked views
messages.manual.fusion.section2.body: CT, PET and FUSION cells are linked; select axial / coronal / sagittal at the top. The fourth cell is **PET MIP**. Drag the locator cross to synchronize position. Use manual registration to adjust alignment.
messages.manual.fusion.section3.title: Fusion 3D
messages.manual.fusion.section3.body: **Fusion 3D** opens a separate tab for CT, PET or fusion. Switching tabs retains the viewpoint. Source registration updates 3D; closing the source keeps the last scene.
messages.manual.registration.title: Manual registration
messages.manual.registration.summary: Keep CT fixed and adjust PET's rigid position and orientation.
messages.manual.registration.caption: CT is fixed; PET is the moving layer.
messages.manual.registration.section0.title: Adjust and verify
messages.manual.registration.section0.body: Choose **Manual registration** in fusion. In PET / FUSION, **left-drag translates and right-drag rotates**, taking priority over default windowing and zoom. Left-drag on the locator cross still repositions the locator. You can also enter parameters; full sampling updates on release. **Check all three orthogonal planes**, not just one direction.
messages.manual.registration.section1.title: Restore and save
messages.manual.registration.section1.body: Use **Align centers, Reset, Load and Save**. Reset restores the initial pairing transform. Registration files store transforms without modifying original DICOM. Loading verifies both source series.
messages.manual.registration.section2.title: Scope
messages.manual.registration.section2.body: Choosing another tool exits registration interaction. Automatic deformable registration is unavailable. Use CT/PET MPR for quantitative segmentation and VOI.
messages.manual.mtf.title: MTF and FWHM analysis
messages.manual.mtf.summary: Independent point-source MTF and wire-ramp FWHM / slice thickness.
messages.manual.mtf.section0.title: 1. Choose a method
messages.manual.mtf.section0.body: **Services → MTF** analyzes in-plane resolution using a bead or perpendicular wire section. The default uses 2D background correction and edge-weighted FFT; MTF50/10 are independent crossings of the measured spectrum. Negative lobes and overshoot are retained. The adjacent **FWHM** tool measures wire-ramp width and slice thickness using Gaussian fit or half-height crossings. Each tool retains its own ROI, analysis settings, results and reset state when switching.
messages.manual.mtf.section1.title: 2. Select and adjust
messages.manual.mtf.section1.body: For a bead or wire section, draw a square ROI of at least 8×8 pixels around one bright target and surrounding background. Center the target with sufficient background; sensitivity warnings indicate that the ROI should be enlarged and checked again. For a ramp, choose **horizontal X / vertical Y** and draw a narrow rectangle along one wire, including background at both ends and at least 8 pixels along the ramp. The ROI controls transverse averaging; rotated or multiple ramps are unsupported. Drag the interior to move or a corner to resize; release to calculate.
messages.manual.mtf.section2.title: 3. Read results
messages.manual.mtf.section2.body: MTF shows X/Y curves and MTF50 / MTF10. FWHM shows half-maximum width and **Slice Thickness = FWHM × tan θ**. Expand **Analysis & profile** to choose Gaussian fitting / half-height crossings and inspect the profile. The default angle is 23°; choose 45° in **Settings → Service tools → FWHM**. Single-ramp results do not correct phantom tilt or substitute nominal DICOM thickness, and do not measure slice spacing. Click **!** for method and quality notes. MTF units are lp/mm or lp/cm; FWHM and thickness use mm.
messages.manual.mtf.section3.title: Limits
messages.manual.mtf.section3.body: Return to the original slice to restore its ROI. **Reset MTF** clears this viewport's results. Finite target size is not corrected. Cross-slice averaging and MPR analysis are unsupported. **No automatic pass/fail assessment is made.**
messages.manual.water-qa.title: CT water phantom QA
messages.manual.water-qa.summary: Analyze five circular ROIs on one water phantom CT slice.
messages.manual.water-qa.caption: Water phantom QA with five ROIs.
messages.manual.water-qa.section0.title: 1. Detect the phantom
messages.manual.water-qa.section0.body: In 2D, choose a complete, near-circular homogeneous water phantom slice and open **Service → QA**. Valid CT pixels and physical spacing are required. Five ROIs are placed at the center and periphery.
messages.manual.water-qa.section1.title: 2. Adjust regions
messages.manual.water-qa.section1.body: Diameter and clearance default to **20 mm** as starting values. Clearance is measured from the outer edge of each peripheral ROI to the phantom boundary. Changing parameters redetects and restores the five baseline ROIs. Drag inside a circle to reposition; release to calculate. All ROIs stay inside the phantom; baseline ROIs cannot overlap each other.
messages.manual.water-qa.section2.title: 3. Read metrics
messages.manual.water-qa.section2.body:
**Water CT number**: center ROI mean.
**Noise**: center ROI population standard deviation.
**Uniformity**: largest absolute peripheral-to-center mean difference.
**Consistency**: range of five ROI means; spatial variation on this slice, not repeatability.
**Horizontal / Vertical difference**: absolute left-right / top-bottom mean difference.
messages.manual.water-qa.section3.title: 4. Read the table
messages.manual.water-qa.section3.body: **Mean, SD and Δcenter** are the ROI mean, population standard deviation and signed difference from the center mean, all in HU. Each row has a duplicate action for an independently movable copy. Only copies can be deleted; the five baseline ROIs are protected. Added ROIs do not contribute to five-ROI summary metrics. Display transforms do not affect statistics.
messages.manual.water-qa.section4.title: Reset and troubleshoot
messages.manual.water-qa.section4.body: Recent slice positions are cached for up to 16 slices. **Reset water phantom QA** clears and stops this viewport's QA. If detection fails, change slice, diameter or margin. Ensure complete ROIs with ≥ 16 pixels. Ordinary measurements and MTF are unaffected.
messages.manual.water-qa.section5.title: No automatic pass/fail result
messages.manual.water-qa.section5.body: Results describe this slice only. Default parameters are not universal acceptance recommendations. Interpret results with the test conditions.
messages.manual.settings.title: Settings and defaults
messages.manual.settings.summary: Open Settings at the bottom left, then search or choose a category.
messages.manual.settings.section0.title: Immediate updates
messages.manual.settings.section0.body: Valid input, sliders and keyboard adjustments apply and save immediately. Incomplete input is not submitted; invalid values revert on Enter or focus loss.
messages.manual.settings.section1.title: Restore defaults
messages.manual.settings.section1.body: **Restore defaults affects only the current category**, and may remove its custom presets. Style preferences do not replace workspace saving.
messages.manual.settings.section2.title: Common settings
messages.manual.settings.section2.body: **Measurements and annotations** sets lines and fonts; **ROI statistics** chooses fields; **Corner information, Crosshairs and Scale bar** controls image overlays.
messages.manual.colormap.title: Color maps and window presets
messages.manual.colormap.summary: Color maps change color; window presets change the display range.
messages.manual.colormap.section0.title: Choose a color map
messages.manual.colormap.section0.body: Set separate defaults for grayscale and PET in Settings. The tool on the right changes the current view; **Tiles synchronizes every cell**. Colors do not change original pixels.
messages.manual.colormap.section1.title: Manage window presets
messages.manual.colormap.section1.body:
Window presets are stored in **window-presets.json**. In **Settings → Window presets**, choose **Open file location**, edit the file, then **Reload presets** without restarting. Existing custom presets and enabled states migrate automatically. Adding, saving or enabling presets in the app writes to the same file. Up to 100 presets are supported. Reloading updates the list without changing the current image window; invalid files leave the current list unchanged and show a reason.

The JSON root contains `schemaVersion: 1` and a `presets` array. Each entry has a unique `presetId`, name `label`, window width `width` (WW), window level `center` (WL), and `enabled`. An empty `label` on a default CT preset uses its translated name; a nonempty label overrides it. Array order controls display order; `enabled: false` hides the entry.

Example entry: `{"presetId":"custom-lung","label":"Lung","width":1500,"center":-600,"enabled":true}`. Width must be 1–1000000, center −1000000–1000000; names must be unique. **MR does not use CT window presets**.
messages.manual.colormap.section2.title: Apply and reset
messages.manual.colormap.section2.body: A preset applies **when clicked**; editing its list does not change the image. Reset 2D windowing to restore initial values. CT 3D uses separate volume presets.
messages.manual.crosshair.title: Crosshair styles
messages.manual.crosshair.summary: A plane's color identifies its intersection in other viewports.
messages.manual.crosshair.section0.title: Crosshair style
messages.manual.crosshair.section0.body: In **Settings → Crosshairs**, set AX/COR/SAG colors and widths. AX color appears in COR and SAG, for example. Slab boundaries follow the plane color. Styling does not move or rotate planes.
messages.manual.crosshair.section1.title: PET fusion locator
messages.manual.crosshair.section1.body: In fusion **Viewport settings**, choose **Small cross / Reference lines** for all four cells. Locator hits take priority for positioning. Switch to the corresponding region tool before editing regions.
messages.manual.corners.title: Viewport overlays
messages.manual.corners.summary: Configure corner information, crosshairs and scale bars.
messages.manual.corners.caption: Select a corner, then arrange its fields.
messages.manual.corners.section0.title: Select and order
messages.manual.corners.section0.body: In **Settings → Corner information**, click a corner preview. Add, remove, search and reorder up to 8 fields per corner. Bottom right includes **Rot / Flip** by default: angle and horizontal / vertical flips. Corner field labels always use English, independent of the interface language. Patient names and series descriptions retain their original content.
messages.manual.corners.section1.title: Text and display
messages.manual.corners.section1.body: Toggle visibility, font size, spacing and color. Small viewports reduce text size and ellipsize each line to prevent overlap. Fusion supports compact or detailed information in viewport settings.
messages.manual.corners.section2.title: View differences
messages.manual.corners.section2.body: **Tiles shows slice numbers only; 3D shows no corner text.** Missing metadata is not invented. These preferences affect display only.
messages.manual.scale.title: Scale bar
messages.manual.scale.summary: The label represents a real physical length.
messages.manual.scale.section0.title: Scale bar size and fitting
messages.manual.scale.section0.body: In **Settings → Scale bar**, choose a maximum of **1, 10, 20, 50 or 100 mm**, default 100 mm. Toggle visibility or change its color. Zoom and window size select a suitable **1, 2, 5 × 10ⁿ mm** length, limited by your setting, 25% of viewport width and 160 px. The scale hides without reliable spacing or enough space.
messages.manual.scale.section1.title: Automatic sizing
messages.manual.scale.section1.body: Zoom and window size select a suitable **1, 2, 5 × 10ⁿ mm** length, limited by your setting, 25% of viewport width and 160 px. The scale hides without reliable spacing or enough space.
messages.manual.export.title: Export images and measurements
messages.manual.export.summary: Choose whether to export a displayed image, source files or results.
messages.manual.export.caption: Anonymization, image exports and measurement reports.
messages.manual.export.section0.title: Current image · PNG
messages.manual.export.section0.body: Right sidebar **Export → Export PNG** saves the active 2D/MPR viewport, the visible montage region, or the current 3D view and crop. Export is unavailable while the view is loading or has failed; all visible montage slices must finish loading. Anonymous export hides application-drawn identity text and text annotations, while preserving measurement lines and arrows.
messages.manual.export.section1.title: Source images · DICOM
messages.manual.export.section1.body: Exports source series and preserves pixels. Fusion saves sources separately; 4D includes phases. **Windowing, measurements, segmentation and cropping are not written into DICOM.** Cancelable tasks publish the output folder on success.
messages.manual.export.section2.title: Whole series and measurements
messages.manual.export.section2.body: **Export series…** at the bottom left saves all DICOM files or per-frame PNGs. Per-frame PNG excludes current viewport transforms and measurements. **CSV report / PDF report** exports completed results; see the report chapter for fields.
messages.manual.export.section3.title: Anonymization
messages.manual.export.section3.body: **Enabled by default**: clears DICOM identity metadata and hides PNG identity text. **Original pixel text and faces are not erased.** Declared identity pixels or embedded overlays cause anonymous export to be refused; check the images. Disabling anonymization retains identity information.
messages.manual.export.section4.title: Find results
messages.manual.export.section4.body: Click the **highlighted result path** to select the file in Finder / File Explorer or open its folder. Hover to read long paths. Canceled or failed exports show a reason.
messages.manual.measurement-report.title: Measurement CSV / PDF
messages.manual.measurement-report.summary: Use CSV for analysis and PDF for reading and sharing.
messages.manual.measurement-report.caption: Export CSV / PDF for the current tab or all tabs.
messages.manual.measurement-report.section0.title: 1. Choose scope
messages.manual.measurement-report.section0.body: Use **Export → CSV report / PDF report**. The default is the current tab; check **Include all tabs** if needed. Finish or cancel editing and wait for VOI statistics first.
messages.manual.measurement-report.section1.title: 2. Check content
messages.manual.measurement-report.section1.body: **CSV** includes type, name, view, slice/phase, plane coordinates and applicable dimensions and statistics. Missing values are blank. **PDF** uses numbered results and optional matched reference images, excluding 3D screenshots. Precision is frozen at export start.
messages.manual.measurement-report.section2.title: 3. Save and locate
messages.manual.measurement-report.section2.body: Choose a location to export in the background. Click the **highlighted file path** to locate it in Finder / File Explorer. Statistics come from pixels or voxels, independently of windowing and color maps.
messages.manual.measurement-report.section3.title: Anonymous scope
messages.manual.measurement-report.section3.body: **Anonymous export** defaults on. It replaces patient and series names and omits IDs, UIDs, paths and free annotation text. Original pixel text is not erased. **A workspace file is not an anonymous report** and should not be shared for the same purpose.
messages.manual.faq.title: Troubleshooting and support
messages.manual.faq.summary: Check the source, view type and current slice first.
messages.manual.faq.section0.title: Why is a button disabled?
messages.manual.faq.section0.body: Select a series and wait for import, then check its modality and format. **MPR/3D require regular volumes; 4D requires valid CT phase groups**. MR 4D playback, fusion and CT analysis tools remain unavailable; PET montage is unavailable. Hover over an entry for its reason, and see **Supported images and formats**.
messages.manual.faq.section1.title: ROI versus VOI
messages.manual.faq.section1.body: Ordinary rectangle / ellipse ROIs provide **2D slice statistics**. MPR segmentation and VOI provide **3D statistics with depth**. 3D cropping changes display only. PET MIP is a projection and is not used to draw 3D regions.
messages.manual.faq.section2.title: Where are my results?
messages.manual.faq.section2.body: Return to the original tab, slice and sampling grid, and check region visibility. Closing tabs releases results. Restore them from a saved workspace.
messages.manual.faq.section3.title: Not yet supported
messages.manual.faq.section3.body: SR import, RTSTRUCT exchange, fractional or LABELMAP SEG, voxel brush editing, contour interpolation and segmentation surfaces are not supported. Binary SEG import/export, SR export and single-layer freehand conversion are supported. Generic multiframe/color viewing, Enhanced PET, Mosaic and MR quantitative analysis remain unavailable. Grayscale Enhanced MR is supported; reconstruction requires regular volumes.

messages.appearance.packsHint: Bundled languages work without local files. Open the folder to export editable copies; restart after adding a new JSON pack.

messages.manual.settings.section3.title: Appearance and language
messages.manual.settings.section3.body: In **Settings → Appearance & language**, choose Light / Dark / Neutral dark or Chinese / English. Changes apply immediately and preserve viewing progress. New installations default to dark and Chinese; preferences persist after restart. Image and measurement colors are independent.
messages.manual.settings.section4.title: Add and edit language packs
messages.manual.settings.section4.body: Open the language pack folder under **Settings → Theme and language**. See **Add a language pack** below for the complete steps and Chinese/English demonstrations.

messages.viewport.error: Display update failed; keeping previous frame: {detail}

messages.manual.tabs.caption: Use the tab bar to choose views, reorder tabs and separate windows.
messages.compare.title: 2D series comparison
messages.compare.empty: No other supported images. Import another series first.
messages.compare.relativeNotice: Relative slice browsing · Images are not registered
messages.compare.independentMeasurements: Measurements and annotations stay with their own image.
messages.compare.scrollHelp: Linked scrolling matches other viewports using the selected mode; otherwise only the active viewport moves.
messages.manual.compare2d.title: 2D and MPR comparison
messages.manual.compare2d.summary: Compare series in 2D or MPR and choose which navigation and display controls to synchronize.
messages.manual.compare2d.section0.title: 2D · Open comparison
messages.manual.compare2d.section0.body: Select **2–4 series** in the sidebar and choose **2D series comparison**. Alternatively, right-click a series and choose 1–3 more. Two series appear side by side; three/four use a four-cell grid. Reopening the same combination activates its existing tab. Press **⌘D (macOS) or Ctrl+D (Windows)**: 2–4 selected series open directly, one opens the picker, and no selection uses the active viewport.
messages.manual.compare2d.section1.title: 2D · Browsing and linking
messages.manual.compare2d.section1.body: Select a viewport and browse with the wheel, **shared slider** or slice controls. New comparisons synchronize display operations by default; if either side is **MR**, **windowing and inversion start independently**. Adjust each option under **Viewport settings → Compare sync operations**. Re-enabling an option uses the selected viewport as the source. With slice sync off, the slider controls only the selected viewport.
messages.manual.compare2d.section2.title: 2D · Patient coordinates and relative progress
messages.manual.compare2d.section2.body: Choose the linking mode in **Viewport settings**. MR defaults to **patient coordinates**: parallel series in the same study and Frame of Reference link within coverage; the shared slider controls the active cell. Cross-plane reference lines and **Alt-click** point navigation are available. Unmatched spaces do not link. **Relative progress** maps different slice counts using the first multi-slice cell; equal progress does not imply the same anatomy. Neither mode performs registration.
messages.manual.compare2d.section3.title: 2D · Measurements, saving and export
messages.manual.compare2d.section3.body: Measurements and annotations remain **independent**, with undo, redo and copy/paste. Current-view export uses the active cell; reports include results from all cells. Workspaces preserve every comparison series, display state, navigation mode and sync option.
messages.mpr.layout.title: MPR layout
messages.mpr.reference.title: 3D spatial reference
messages.mpr.reference.hint: Drag the 3D center marker to move the MPR intersection. With rotation linked, rotating 3D also rotates the MPR planes.
messages.manual.mpr.section4.title: Choose a layout
messages.manual.mpr.section4.body: Choose horizontal/vertical triplets, a large left/right/top/bottom plane, or four views including 3D in **MPR layout**. The default is a large right plane. CT, MR, standalone PET MPR and CT 4D support all seven layouts. Switching preserves slices, windows, measurements and annotations; double-click temporarily maximizes a plane. Fusion retains its own layout. Double-click a slice or the 3D cell to maximize it within the viewing area; double-click again to restore the layout without changing the camera or preset.
messages.manual.mpr.section5.title: Four views and 3D positioning
messages.manual.mpr.section5.body: The four-view layout places axial at the top left, coronal at the top right, sagittal at the bottom left and a 3D reference at the bottom right. It reuses the current MPR volume and follows 4D phase changes. Colored outlines mark the intersection of each plane with the volume bounds, using the crosshair colors. A cyan ring marks their common intersection and remains visible inside the volume. Choose intersection only or hide the reference if desired. The outlines mark individual planes, not the full slab thickness. Enable Remember layout to reuse this layout for new views of the same type and remember subsequent changes. MPR and 4D keep separate preferences. Disabling it leaves the current view unchanged and uses the default for new views. Workspace restoration uses each saved tab layout without overwriting the preference.
messages.manual.mpr.section6.title: 3D interaction and linked rotation
messages.manual.mpr.section6.body: Click the 3D cell or its title to select it. The right toolbar switches to rotation, pan, zoom, display presets (display settings for PET), six viewing directions, export and reset. Click an MPR plane to return to its tools. Both toolbars provide separate View layout and Viewport settings controls. Drag near the cyan ring to move the MPR intersection in the current camera plane, within the volume bounds. **Link 3D and MPR rotation** is enabled by default: the reconstructed planes and camera rotate together in either direction. Turn it off in **Viewport settings** to rotate independently. Pan and zoom remain independent. Layout, active viewport, each tool selection, reference mode, rotation linking and the 3D camera are saved with the workspace. In a 4D tab, the selected 3D view also retains **4D Play**. The collapsed toolbar also provides presets, six view directions, layout, and viewport settings controls. Presets open a named list; directions expand into secondary buttons. Reference planes and rotation linking are configured in **Viewport settings**. The 3D label identifies the target view. Reset 3D view resets its camera and display; enabled rotation linking still propagates camera rotation to MPR. Presets match the modality and are independent of slice windowing. The 3D name appears inside the upper-left corner, follows corner-information visibility, font size and color, and uses no separate header row. CT / MR axial, coronal and sagittal windows are linked; 3D windowing and presets remain independent.
messages.layout.title: View layout
messages.layout.dragHint: Choose rows and columns; drag a series into a viewport.
messages.manual.2d.section4.title: Layouts and drag and drop
messages.manual.2d.section4.body: The first **Layout** tool offers single, row, column, grid and main-view layouts, plus a custom grid up to **6 × 6**. New cells are empty. Drag a series from the sidebar, including its collapsed thumbnail rail, into a cell to load or replace it. Click a cell to target the right toolbar. Smaller layouts hide extra cells and expanding restores them; double-click an image to temporarily maximize it. Window sizes use logical pixels. The main window defaults to **1440 × 900**, with a **1280 × 720** minimum. Detached windows default to **1120 × 840**, with a **960 × 720** minimum. At least **640 × 520** is reserved for the central reading area, excluding tabs; panel resizing respects this space. Windows fit the available desktop and temporarily compact panels when necessary, restoring preferences when space returns. Very small screens reduce the minimum to their available space. Multiple viewports share the central area; double-click an image to focus it.
messages.manual.2d.section5.title: Original slices and reconstructed planes
messages.manual.2d.section5.body: Use the selector in the upper-left corner of each 2D viewport to choose **Original slices, Axial MPR, Coronal MPR or Sagittal MPR**. Original slices retain their acquisition orientation, with the actual plane (including Oblique) alongside. Reconstructed planes use the current series volume, without switching source series. Their position appears alongside without repeating the plane name. Positions retain S/I, L/R, P/A and mm; hover for an explanation. These are not slice thicknesses or slice numbers. Missing spatial information is shown as unavailable. Incomplete volume data produces an error inside the cell; Original slices remains available. Each mode retains its own slice, window, zoom and measurements. The workspace restores cell sources, modes and layout. The selector remains available when corner information is hidden.
messages.manual.2d.section6.title: Compact right toolbar
messages.manual.2d.section6.body: Click the arrow beside the bottom reset area to collapse the tools into a **44-pixel** rail. It retains available window/level, scroll, pan, zoom and 3D rotation tools. Click **Measure, Rotate, Annotate or Pseudocolor** to reveal action icons beneath the button. Click again to collapse; opening another group closes the previous one. Secondary actions use a distinct background and spacing. **Reset all** at the bottom matches the primary reset in the expanded toolbar: it restores the current view and clears its corresponding measurements and annotations. With the toolbar expanded, the reset beneath the detail panel remains scoped to the active tool. Click **Play** to loop through the active view’s slices; click again to stop at the current position. Both expanded and collapsed toolbars offer Play / Stop. Set 1–15 FPS in the expanded panel. Switching views or tabs stops playback; single images cannot play.
messages.viewport.scope.title: Apply to
messages.viewport.scope.currentHint: Change only the active cell; its orientation modes keep these settings.
messages.viewport.scope.tabHint: Apply to all cells, including new ones. A dash indicates mixed settings.
messages.manual.2d.section7.title: Viewport display settings
messages.manual.2d.section7.body: Choose **Active viewport** or **Entire tab** in **Viewport settings → Apply to**. Control corner information, patient privacy, scale and color bars, orientation markers and fit to window. Entire tab includes hidden cells; new cells inherit its settings. Other tabs are unaffected. A dash indicates mixed settings; click to set all cells on or off. **Orientation markers** are patient direction letters such as A/P, R/L and H/F. Original slices and independent reconstructed 2D cells have no linked crosshair, so their settings omit Localizer. MPR retains this option.
messages.compare.mpr.title: MPR series comparison
messages.compare.mpr.layoutHint: Double-click a slice to enlarge the matching pair; double-click again to return to six views.
messages.compare.mpr.linkHint: Independent by default. Position each series first, then link subsequent movement or rotation. This does not register the images.
messages.manual.comparempr.title: MPR series comparison
messages.manual.comparempr.summary: Two independent MPR groups with six views and optional position and rotation linking.
messages.manual.comparempr.section0.title: MPR · Open six views
messages.manual.comparempr.section0.body: Select two reconstructable series in the sidebar and choose **MPR series comparison** from the context menu, or start from one series and select its partner. Both series must form regular volumes. The **MPR Compare** tab shows A above B, with Axial, Coronal and Sagittal columns.
messages.manual.comparempr.section1.title: MPR · Independent controls and paired enlargement
messages.manual.comparempr.section1.body: Click a plane to activate it; the right toolbar follows its group. Position, rotation, windowing, zoom and pan are independent between groups by default. The three planes within a group share their spatial position, and CT windowing is synchronized within that group. Double-click a plane to enlarge its corresponding pair side by side; double-click again to return to six views. The first **Layout** tool also selects these arrangements.
messages.manual.comparempr.section2.title: MPR · Position and rotation links
messages.manual.comparempr.section2.body: Enable **Link position** and **Link rotation** separately in **Layout**. Both are off by default. Position each group first; enabling a link does not jump or align the images. Subsequent displacement (in patient-coordinate millimetres) or rotation from either group is applied to the other, preserving their existing relative offset. Disable a link to resume independent control. This feature performs **no automatic registration**; linked motion does not establish anatomical correspondence.
messages.manual.comparempr.section3.title: MPR · Independent measurements and workspace recovery
messages.manual.comparempr.section3.body: Each plane owns its measurements and annotations, with undo, redo, copy and paste. Reports retain the source series for each result. Saving a workspace preserves both image references, plane positions and orientations, display states, measurements, annotations, active viewport, enlarged pair and link settings. Original images must remain accessible when restoring.
messages.compare.mpr.displaySyncHint: Enabling uses the active series. Window linking requires two CT series and preserves each inversion setting. Zoom matches millimetres on corresponding planes.
messages.compare.mpr.outsideHint: This section does not intersect the series. Move the crosshair or return to the series centre.
messages.compare.mpr.zoomLimit: The field-of-view difference exceeds the zoom range. Scale linking was turned off.
messages.manual.comparempr.section4.title: MPR · Persistent link status and display linking
messages.manual.comparempr.section4.body: Position, rotation, CT windowing and physical-scale controls stay visible above the comparison, even with the right toolbar collapsed. Highlighted buttons are on; hover to inspect their state or configure them in Layout. Window linking requires two CT series and adopts the active series WW / WL while preserving each inversion setting. Physical-scale linking matches millimetres on corresponding planes; zoom multipliers may differ. Matching persists across layout and window-size changes. All four options default to off and are saved with the workspace.
messages.manual.comparempr.section5.title: MPR · Outside the image range
messages.manual.comparempr.section5.body: **Outside image range** appears when the finite section or slab does not intersect this series volume. Detection uses geometry, so ordinary black image backgrounds do not trigger it. Move the crosshair or choose **Return this series to centre**. Recovery moves only that series and preserves the other position and all link settings.
messages.mr.unsupportedFormat: Classic single-frame and grayscale Enhanced MR are supported; this MR object format is unsupported.
messages.mr.unsupportedPixels: MR viewing currently supports single-channel MONOCHROME1 / MONOCHROME2 images.
messages.mr.mixedDimensions: This MR series contains different echoes, diffusion encodings, time points or image types. Use 2D or montage; a single MPR volume cannot be built.
messages.mr.geometry: MR MPR requires at least two regular slices with consistent matrix, orientation and spacing, and no duplicate positions. Use 2D or montage.
messages.mr.localizer: MR localizers cannot be reconstructed with MPR. Use 2D or montage.
messages.mr.unsupportedView: MR 4D playback and fusion are not supported yet.
messages.mr.mixedUnits: MR images with different intensity units cannot be combined into one volume.
messages.mr.invalidWindow: Window width must be 0.001–1000000 and level must be -1000000–1000000.
messages.manual.mr.title: Basic MR viewing
messages.manual.mr.summary: Classic and Enhanced MR grouping, windowing, spatial comparison, MPR and 3D.
messages.manual.mr.section0.title: Open, group and window
messages.manual.mr.section0.body: Classic single-frame and grayscale **Enhanced MR / Legacy Converted Enhanced MR** are supported. Echoes, b-values, diffusion directions, time points, components and dimension indices form separate display groups, labeled in the list. Sources remain unchanged. **2D** opens at the middle slice using its DICOM window, or an estimated range if absent. Scrolling retains the window; **Auto window** recalculates it from the current image. Inputs support three decimals.
messages.manual.mr.section1.title: Acquisition parameters and measurements
messages.manual.mr.section1.body: The overlay shows available **TR, TE, TI, FA, B0 and b-value**. Enhanced MR uses shared/per-frame geometry and pixel scaling. Length, angle and ROI tools work as usual. Unspecified intensity units are **a.u.**, never HU or SUV. Real World Value Mapping and vendor-private quantitative conversion are not implemented. CT windows, water QA, MTF, threshold segmentation and VOI are hidden for MR.
messages.manual.mr.section2.title: MPR and multi-series comparison
messages.manual.mr.section2.body: Regular stacks support **MPR** with linked position, window and inversion across three planes and seven layouts. The initial window uses the whole volume to avoid narrow peripheral-slice windows. Compare **2–4 series** with independent MR windows and patient-coordinate linking by default. Parallel stacks in the same reference space scroll together within coverage. Cross-plane reference lines and **Alt-click** point navigation are available. Different spaces remain independent; no registration is performed.
messages.manual.mr.section3.title: MR 3D
messages.manual.mr.section3.body: Regular MR volumes use the existing **3D** tab or four-view MPR layout. **MR grayscale volume, MR high signal and MR MIP** provide float windowing, auto window, rotation, zoom, directions, cropping and screenshots. Presets use this volume’s intensity range, without CT HU thresholds. Thin, nearly isotropic data is better suited to 3D; interpolation cannot restore missing through-plane detail.
messages.mr.mosaic: This MR uses mosaic storage. Slice unpacking is not supported, so viewing and measurement are unavailable. The DICOM tags can be inspected.
messages.manual.supported-images.title: Supported images and formats
messages.manual.supported-images.summary: Check input requirements, views and tools for CT, MR and PET.
messages.manual.supported-images.section0.title: CT: classic single-frame and Enhanced CT
messages.manual.supported-images.section0.body: Supports classic CT, Enhanced CT and Legacy Converted Enhanced CT. Shared/per-frame metadata supplies geometry, windows and rescale; time points and other dimensions form separate groups. Regular HU grayscale volumes support **2D, Montage, comparison, MPR and 3D**. Non-HU/supplemental-color derived images support frame browsing and quantitative measurements, without HU analysis or volume reconstruction. **4D** currently uses multiple classic CT phase series.
messages.manual.supported-images.section1.title: MR: classic and Enhanced MR
messages.manual.supported-images.section1.body: Classic **MR Image Storage**, **Enhanced MR** and **Legacy Converted Enhanced MR** support single-sample MONOCHROME1/MONOCHROME2. Shared/per-frame metadata drives decoding and display groups. Use existing **2D, montage, 2–4-series comparison, MPR and 3D** tabs. MR has auto window, source units and basic measurements; CT-specific templates and analysis are hidden.
messages.manual.supported-images.section2.title: MR reconstruction and quantitative limits
messages.manual.supported-images.section2.body: MPR/3D require one echo, diffusion encoding, time point and component with regular geometry. Missing dimensions are not guessed; localizers, duplicate positions and irregular slices cannot be reconstructed. **MR Color, Mosaic, spectroscopy, MR 4D playback and fusion** remain unsupported. DWI/ADC may be displayed when their format is supported, without ADC calculation, Real World Value Mapping, vendor-private quantitative scaling, DTI, perfusion or fMRI analysis.
messages.manual.supported-images.section3.title: PET: classic static or whole-body PT
messages.manual.supported-images.section3.body: Supports classic **PET Image Storage**, single-frame **MONOCHROME2**, with SeriesType **STATIC / IMAGE** or **WHOLE BODY / IMAGE**. Available views are **2D, Compare 2D, MPR and 3D**, plus fusion and fusion 3D for eligible CT / PET pairs. Units depend on metadata; missing required information prevents SUV conversion. PET Montage, 4D, dynamic / gated and Enhanced / multi-frame PET are unsupported.
messages.manual.supported-images.section4.title: Other objects and multi-frame data
messages.manual.supported-images.section4.body: CR, DX, US and XA have not completed dedicated validation; some decodable single-frame grayscale images use generic 2D viewing. **Tag** access does not imply full viewing support. Associated results support binary SEG import/export and SR export; SR import and RTSTRUCT exchange are not implemented.
messages.manual.supported-images.section5.title: File formats and pixel decoding
messages.manual.supported-images.section5.body: The **.dcm** extension is optional. ZIP, RAR, 7z and TAR are outer archives containing supported DICOM objects. The application bundles decoders for uncompressed pixels, RLE, JPEG Baseline/Extended (8-bit only)/Lossless, JPEG-LS and JPEG 2000. Viewing, thumbnails and PNG export share the same decoder policy. Missing components, unsupported encodings and decoding failures have distinct messages. Pixel decoding support does not imply support for all multi-frame, color or video objects. **NIfTI (.nii / .nii.gz), NRRD and vendor raw MR data** are not supported inputs.
messages.mr.invalidFrames: Enhanced MR frame metadata is incomplete or invalid; inspect the source in Tag.
messages.compare.spatialNotice: Patient coordinates: scrolling links parallel stacks within coverage in the same space. Alt-click locates other planes; no registration is performed.
messages.compare.unlinkedSpace: No comparison series shares the active patient space. Browse independently or select relative progress.
messages.mr.frameExportNotice: PNG exports only this display group. DICOM preserves complete source objects, which may also contain other echoes, time points or components.
messages.manual.mr.section4.title: Export and current limits
messages.manual.mr.section4.body: **PNG** exports the selected display group. **DICOM** preserves complete source objects, possibly including other echoes, time points or components. Tag shows the complete source file. Mosaic, MR Color, spectroscopy, MR 4D playback, fusion and quantitative analysis are unsupported. Missing dimension information is not guessed; duplicate positions, localizers and irregular geometry cannot enter MPR/3D. Viewing DWI/ADC is not ADC calculation, DTI, perfusion or fMRI analysis.
messages.manual.volume.section5.title: MR volume rendering
messages.manual.volume.section5.body: MR provides grayscale, high-signal and MIP presets using the current volume’s intensity range. Auto/manual windows support three decimals. Rotation, zoom, directions, cropping and PNG export use the existing 3D tools. CT tissue presets and table removal are hidden. Volume rendering is not a segmented tissue model. MR MIP auto-window uses the full finite intensity range to reduce clipping in maximum projections.

messages.manual.measurement.section4.title: Freehand ROI
messages.manual.measurement.section4.body: Select **Freehand ROI** and click to place control points. A smooth closed curve passes through them. Pointer movement only previews the boundary. Click the first point, double-click or press `Enter` to finish; `Esc` cancels. Drag controls to reshape or the interior to move. Area, perimeter, pixel statistics and segmentation conversion use the smooth boundary. At least three points are required. Clicks or drags that would cross the contour leave the last valid shape unchanged. Existing polygon ROIs retain their original outlines.
messages.manual.segmentation.section4.title: Export SEG
messages.manual.segmentation.section4.body: Finish segmentation and wait for statistics, then choose **Export → Export SEG**. Regions in this tab and phase on the same source grid share a binary multi-segment SEG, retaining overlaps. Large collections are batched within a memory budget. Adjust empty regions before exporting.
messages.manual.export.section5.title: SEG and structured SR
messages.manual.export.section5.body: Use **DICOM segmentation and structured report** to export SEG or SR. Each SEG has its own segmentation statistics SR. Lengths, angles and ROIs produce a separate planar measurement SR; studies remain separate. Patient identity and source references are retained; anonymization above does not apply. Slicer 5.12.4 has limitations reading planar measurement SR; export PDF/CSV for viewing.
messages.manual.measurement-report.section4.title: Structured measurements · DICOM SR
messages.manual.measurement-report.section4.body: **Export SR** produces a TID 1500 report retaining numeric precision, units, locations, tracking identifiers and source references. Native 2D images use image coordinates; MPR uses patient coordinates; VOIs/segments reference SEG. Reports are preliminary and unverified. Projection measurements and results without a verified source coordinate mapping stop export with an explanation.

messages.seg.roiPlane: Conversion requires a plane parallel to the native voxel grid. Oblique ROIs are not supported yet.

messages.manual.segmentation.section5.title: Import and manage SEG
messages.manual.segmentation.section5.body: Import source DICOM on the left, open its MPR / 4D tab and phase, then choose **Import → Import SEG segmentation** on the right. Native-grid binary SEG supports multiple and overlapping segments. Use **Manage segments** to rename, recolor, show, hide or delete them, with undo and workspace persistence. Imported mask geometry is fixed. MR supports segment management too.
messages.manual.measurement.section5.title: Convert freehand ROI to segmentation
messages.manual.measurement.section5.body: Select a completed freehand ROI in MPR / 4D and choose **Convert to segmentation**. Native voxel centers create one layer nearest the current plane, retaining the measurement without extending across slices. Oblique and projected contours are unsupported. Later contour edits do not update the mask, which can be saved and exported as SEG.

messages.manual.measurement.section6.body: Select **Curve** and click to place at least three control points. Double-click or press `Enter` to finish; `Esc` cancels. The open smooth curve passes through its controls and reports physical arc length. Drag controls to edit. Clicks or drags that would cross or retrace the path leave the last valid curve unchanged. messages.manual.language-packs.title: Add a language pack
messages.manual.language-packs.summary: Add a JSON file to the local language folder, then restart and select it. The manual follows the interface language.
messages.manual.language-packs.caption: Open the language folder, add Español, and select it after restarting.
messages.manual.language-packs.section0.title: 1. Open the language folder
messages.manual.language-packs.section0.body: Go to **Settings → Theme and language** and click **Open language pack folder**. Missing editable copies of the bundled languages are exported. Existing files are preserved.
messages.manual.language-packs.section1.title: 2. Prepare a new language file
messages.manual.language-packs.section1.body: For Spanish, copy `en-US.json` and name the copy `es-ES.json`. In the copy, change `locale` to `es-ES` and `name` to `Español`. The filename must match `locale`; keep `formatVersion` set to `1`.
messages.manual.language-packs.section2.title: 3. Translate the text
messages.manual.language-packs.section2.body: Use a text editor and save the JSON as **UTF-8**. Translate the text inside `messages`, keeping message IDs, placeholder names and formats intact. You can translate a few entries first; missing translations use English. Manual text is included in the pack. Preserve `**emphasis**` and backticks around shortcuts.
messages.manual.language-packs.section3.title: 4. Restart and select
messages.manual.language-packs.section3.body: Save the file, restart the app, and select **Español** under **Settings → Theme and language**. The change applies immediately and is remembered on the next launch. After editing an existing pack, you can also click **Reload language packs**.
messages.manual.language-packs.section4.title: Switch the manual between Chinese and English
messages.manual.language-packs.section4.body: Select **Simplified Chinese** or **English** under **Settings → Theme and language**. The manual navigation, text, search results, screenshots and this tutorial animation switch together without restarting.
messages.manual.language-packs.section5.title: Bundled languages and errors
messages.manual.language-packs.section5.body: Chinese, English and Brazilian Portuguese (`pt-BR`) are bundled and can be selected without local copies. Edited local packs take priority; missing entries use the bundled language, or English for a new language. Invalid JSON or placeholders are reported in Settings and preserve the current valid text. Correct the file and reload, or remove the local copy to restore the bundled content.

messages.manual.settings.updates.title: Software updates
messages.manual.settings.updates.body: Enable or disable startup checks in **Settings → Software updates**; checks are on by default. When a stable release is available, review its release notes and select **Download and update**. The app downloads and verifies the package, follows your workspace save preference, then exits, installs, and restarts. Cancelling suppresses reminders for that version; the badge beside the version number lets you continue later. You can also **Check for updates** manually. Automatic installation supports macOS arm64 applications and Windows x64 installers and single-file portable builds. Source and folder-portable builds use the downloads page. Check failures are silent; failed installation restores the previous version.

messages.manual.measurement-edit.p0.title: Measurement list
messages.manual.measurement-edit.p0.body: **Measure → Measurements** lists completed measurements across every view, slice and phase of the current tab. Select an entry to return to its source. Rename, show/hide, lock or delete entries. Locking protects both geometry and metric cards; copies are independent and unlocked. Hidden measurements remain in reports. Names, visibility and locks support undo and workspace saving.
messages.manual.mtf.p0.title: Save and recalculate
messages.manual.mtf.p0.body: Workspaces retain completed MTF/FWHM ROIs, curves, results and calculation parameters. Reopening or changing global calculation settings does not recompute saved results. Select **Recalculate** to use current settings; units and precision only affect formatting. The information button shows application and algorithm versions and calculation time. Source mismatches retain historical records without displaying an overlay.
messages.manual.water-qa.p0.title: Save QA results
messages.manual.water-qa.p0.body: Workspaces save complete per-slice QA results, including the five adjusted baseline ROIs and additional copies. Reopening retains saved values. **Recalculate** checks the current slice, retaining ROI positions and copies when settings are unchanged. Results are not reused when source pixels or geometry differ; failed calculations do not overwrite the last successful record.
messages.manual.measurement-report.p0.title: Matched reference images
messages.manual.measurement-report.p0.body: PDF reference images are enabled by default and rendered from each measurement’s slice, phase and reconstruction plane without changing your current view. Measurements sharing the same view, phase and sampling plane share an image with matching numbered labels. Rendering uses the window and colour map at export start. Unavailable references retain their values with an explanation; the current slice is never substituted. Progress and cancellation are available.

messages.manual.settings.feedback.title: Help & feedback
messages.manual.settings.feedback.body: Open **Help & feedback** at the bottom of Settings navigation or the manual contents. Enter a title and description, review the optional system information, then choose **Open GitHub** or **Email**. GitHub opens a prefilled issue; email opens a draft addressed to **5769389@qq.com**. Review and submit it yourself. Long feedback is copied in full for pasting into the draft; you can also copy feedback or the address directly. System information excludes patient data, images, file paths and logs. Add screenshots manually and hide patient details first. Use **Add attachments** for images, DICOM, PDF, ZIP or other regular files (up to 32 files, 25 MiB total). Check patient information and confirm sharing, then **Email** requests a system composer with attachments for you to review and send. macOS uses its email sharing service; Windows requires a MAPI-compatible mail client. Otherwise, **Save email file** (.eml) and edit or forward it in your mail client. Mail providers may impose lower size limits, and attachment encoding increases message size. Attachments are not automatically anonymized or uploaded to GitHub. You can also leave the fields empty and choose **Open GitHub** to write your feedback on the website.
